content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, rule T4C).**

**What the document says.** The term/termination article sits in §4 (inside the surfaced §1.4 block):
- **§4.1** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other."
- **§4.2** — if *the Company* terminates, it owes HDI a "Termination Payment" equal to (12 months' Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, payable in eight quarterly installments.

**Why it deviates.**
1. Our only convenience exit costs 90 days' notice *and* a penalty — the playbook requires 30 days without penalty and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
2. The Termination Payment is uncapped and economically severe: 50% of Net Sales above $800,000, versus the 30%-of-Net-Sales fee we actually pay under §3.1. That can dwarf the fallback ceiling of three months' fees.
3. HDI's convenience right is symmetrical and, read literally, is not confined to the end of a term — the vendor should not be able to walk mid-term.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level).** Amended §4.1 to add a Company 30-day convenience right (in whole or in part) with refund of prepaid fees, and to confine HDI's convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice; replaced §4.2(a) with an express no-penalty statement and deleted the now-orphaned subsections (b) and (c). The comment offers the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees if HDI needs exit compensation.
